blocks.x: Amid a sea of rising hardware prices, it's easy to lose sight of your gaming setup necessities. It's all very well and good having a rip roaring rig, but if you've got nowhere to comfortably park your keister through long hours of gaming, then what's the point? Thankfully, my beady little eyes have spotted more than a few excellent gaming chair deals this Prime Day.

Hey, if you've been going full prawn mode in an inexpensive perch, you'll find no judgment here—we've all been there. But if you're looking for your first gaming chair, it's well worth reading what Ridley recommends here, and then taking a gander at what we reckon are the best gaming chairs in 2026 here. For instance, the Secretlab Titan Evo is the best gaming chair overall. Now it's down to $579 when you buy directly, so it might be time to treat yourself to an upgrade.

But you don't have to spend over half a grand for superior posterior comfort. The Corsair TC100 Relaxed was our budget pick for a long old while, and now that you can get the leatherette version for only $154 and the fabric version for just under $200, it's definitely worth considering again.
We're curating all the best Prime Day PC gaming deals here

If neither of those float your boat, (or, as the case may be, your buns) there are plenty more gaming chair deals to consider. The basic version of the Razer Iskur V2 X gaming chair is currently down to $220 in the Prime Day sales, with the Newgen version a smidge more expensive at $240. Personally, I'm waiting for the Cinnamoroll colourway to come down in price, but I fear I might be waiting a while…

Parting with hundreds of smackers for a chair can feel like a lot, but it's worth it if it saves your back from plenty of pain. Furthermore, if you want to ditch the more gamer-y stylings for something a little more office chic, you can get the lumbar supporting ThunderX3 XTC in a fetching pale blue or grey mesh for only $120.

I reckon the Fractal Design Refine also wouldn't look out of place in an office (especially for just under $500), though I hear it's less comfortable for bigger folk. Not to worry, because there are plenty more deals for folks of all sizes and budgets below.

Though not as swish as our pick for the best office chair, the ThunderX3 Flex Pro, the XTC offers similarly lovely lumbar support. Add to that synchronous tilt, 3D armrests, and adjustable seat depth, and this could still be one comfy customer.
Key specs: Breathable mesh | 3D armrests | Self-adjusting backrest and lumbar supportView Deal

TC100 Relaxed: was $269.99 now $199.99
The TC100 was our most favorite affordable gaming chair for a long old while, following up on the popular T3 Rush with a great look and genuine comfort. You can read more in our review. It's a truly excellent gaming chair that's cheaper than most of its competition especially in the Prime Day sales.
Key specs: Fabric | 2D armrests
Price check: Corsair $199.99 | B&H $269.99 | Newegg $310.99View Deal

If you want a pink throne then this is for you. It also comes in black, by the way, but where's the fun in that? We've been fans of the Razer Enki line-up in the past and this model is a high-quality unit. The 4D armrests, recline and lumbar support all help to get it snugly fitted around your frame, which we like to see for this sorta money.
Key specs: 4D armrests | Multiple colors availableView Deal

Fractal Design makes a mean PC case, and it recently turned its gaze towards the world of gaming chairs with the Refine. It's a comfortable chair with a good look, as you can read about in my review, though it's not ideal for bigger bodies.
Key specs: 4D armrests
Price check: B&H Photo $499.99 (Black Fabric version)View Deal

TC500 Luxe Gaming Chair: was $549.99 now $441.14
It seems like a simple deal to make the most of, but your entire body will thank you once you've got support in all the right places. Make the hours you already spend tethered to your setup even more comfortable with the TC500 Luxe.
Key specs: Omniflex armrests | Built-in lumbar support | Detachable neck pillow
Price check: Corsair $549.99View Deal

Titan Evo 2022: $579
The overall style might look a little dated now, but that's mostly down to competitors 'borrowing' Secretlab's classic design. It's the best gaming chair you can buy, and we don't say such things lightly.
Key specs: Leatherette | 4D armrests | Magnetic head pillow
Price check: Amazon $669View Deal
